name: Europe

meta.title: Study in Europe from India: Germany, Malta, Ireland compared
meta.description: Compare studying in Germany, Malta and Ireland: tuition, money to show for the visa, work during study and how long you can stay after graduating.

summary: Low-fee public universities in Germany, part-time work in Malta, and up to 2 years of stay-back in Ireland.

whyReasons.text: Germany's public universities charge no tuition for most bachelor's and master's programmes. You pay a semester contribution of €70 to €430.
Graduates in Germany get up to 18 months to find a job. Malta gives a one-time 9-month permit. Ireland gives master's graduates up to 24 months.
A residence permit from one Schengen country such as Germany or Malta lets you travel to other Schengen countries for short visits. Ireland is not in the Schengen area.

faq.q: Which European country is cheapest to study in?
faq.a: Germany's public universities charge no tuition for most courses, but you must show €11,904 a year for living costs. Your counsellor will compare total costs for your course across Germany, Malta and Ireland.

faq.q: Do I need German to study in Germany?
faq.a: Not for every course. Some programmes are taught fully in English. Check the teaching language of each course on your shortlist; the DAAD course database lets you filter by language.

faq.q: Can I work after studying in Europe?
faq.a: Germany gives graduates up to 18 months to look for work, Ireland up to 24 months after a master's, and Malta a one-time 9-month permit.
